newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London -- 300 turbulent years.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London -- 300 turbulent years.

text.p: Lloyd's of London, which appeared poised on Wednesday to win the necessary support from its members to complete a recovery plan, is the oldest insurance market in the world. It dates back to the late 17th Century and a coffee house in the City of London's Tower Street.
A chronology of the important event's in Lloyd's history follows:
1996 August -- A U.S. appeals court overturns a ruling that had threatened the insurance market's survival.

July -- Names vote overwhelmingly to raise a special 440 million pound contribution for R&R -- Reconstruction and Renewal -- from those underwriting in the last three years. R&R is the vehicle for restructuring the market.
July -- overall profit of 1,084 million pounds for 1993
July -- agreement with U.S. states that they end action against Lloyd's in return for extra financial help for Names
May -- Lloyd's increases settlement offer to 3.2 billion
February -- Sale and leaseback of Lloyd's building pounds ($4.98 billion) from 2.8 billion pounds. 1995 November -- Peter Middleton resigns and Ron Sandler appointed chief executive
October -- Merrett Names win negligence judgment
May -- Reconstruction and Renewal plan announced, including 2.8 billion pounds settlement offer
May -- Treasury and Civil Service Select Committee on financial services regulation publishes report on Lloyd's
May -- overall loss of 1,193 million pounds in 1992
March -- Feltrim Names win negligence judgement 1994 December -- 900 million pounds settlement offer
October -- Members vote to admit corporate capital
October -- Gooda Walker Names win negligence judgement
June -- overall loss of 2,319 million pounds for 1990 1992 September -- Peter Middleton appointed chief executive
September -- Hurricane Andrew
June -- overall loss of 1,863 million pounds for 1989
April -- Outhwaite settlement (116 million pounds)
February -- inquiry into reinsurance spiral begins 1991 September -- Typhoon Mirelle (Japan)
July -- Gooda Walker and Feltrim action groups formed
June -- overall loss of 510 million pounds for 1988 1990 July -- Colorado storms
June -- overall profit of 509 million pounds for 1987
January/February -- European storms 1989 October -- Philips Pasadena refinery explosion
October -- San Francisco earthquake
September -- Hurricane Hugo
March -- Exxon Valdez oil tanker disaster 1988 December -- Lockerbie PanAm Boeing 747 disaster in Scotland.

July -- Piper Alpha oil rig explosion 1986 May -- business commences in new Lloyd's building 1973 -- Capacity reaches 1,045 million pounds, women members allowed to work in the "room" 1968 -- First overall loss of 37.9 million pounds for 1965 1958 -- Market transfers to new Lime Street building 1880s -- First Lloyd's reinsurance policy on American risks 1871 -- Lloyd's incorporated in Act of Parliament 1844 -- Lloyd's market returns to rebuilt Royal Exchange 1838 -- Royal Exchange destroyed by fire 1774 -- Rooms rented in the Royal Exchange 1734 -- "Lloyd's List" established as weekly publication 1688 -- First reference to Edward Lloyd's coffee house ($1=.6421 Pound)
